video_description:
President Donald Trump said in an interview Friday that he expects to make more Cabinet changes in the wake of the GOP’s midterm rout – suggesting chief of staff Susie Wiles is not the only person to be replaced.

Speaking to Ross Douthat with CBS News for an interview that is set to air Sunday on 60 Minutes, Trump responded “I do” when asked if he expected to fire people. A clip of the interview aired on CBS Evening News.

brief:
Summary: President Donald Trump is reacting to a major GOP defeat in the midterms, blaming the losses while claiming he was not on the ballot. Following the election wipeout, Susie Wiles is stepping down as White House Chief of Staff and being replaced immediately by Stephen Miller. Correspondents and analysts discuss Trump's frustration, his potential pivot toward more aggressive and extreme policies, and the possibility of further Cabinet firings.
People: Donald Trump; Susie Wiles; Stephen Miller; Ross Douthat; Nancy LaCour; Nancy Mace; Jenny Costa Honeycutt; Ashley Moody; Byron Donalds; Julia Benbrook; Robert De Niro; James Talerico
Context: A news broadcast reporting on the fallout of a midterm election defeat for Republicans, focusing on White House staff changes, Donald Trump's speech at the Kennedy Space Center, and an upcoming CBS News 60 Minutes interview with Ross Douthat.
